page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by Alibaba's in-house YiTian710 processor running at 2.75 GHz, providing 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (4 vCPUs total). The architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 64 MB L3 cache pool. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage and connects to cloud networks via a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark results show balanced compute and read throughput alongside specific bottlenecks. The instance achieves average mid-tier scores in stress-ng single-core (1819.58) and multi-core (7234.41) tests. Memory read bandwidth is competitive, reaching 409.68 GB/sec on cached 16 KB blocks and 59.55 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks. However, uncached write memory bandwidth drops into the lower tier at 24.45 GB/sec. General compute metrics from PassMark show weak overall ratings (3466.43), driven by weak extended instruction results and poor encryption performance (654.15). In application tests, it handles in-memory operations steadily, executing 6.4 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining mid-tier database operation scores.

Given its ARM-based architecture and substantial memory density, the ecs.r8y.xlarge is well-aligned with in-memory caching tiers such as Redis or Memcached, as well as moderate relational and analytical databases that fit entirely in memory. Workloads relying heavily on heavy cryptographic operations, high uncached memory write throughput, or x86 instruction extensions should take note of its architectural tradeoffs. Because local storage is absent, all persistent storage depends on network-attached block devices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the arm64 Alibaba YiTian710 processor, offering 4 dedicated cores clocked at 2.75 GHz with 32.0 GB of memory and no bundled local storage. Providing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the system features a 64 MB L3 cache and a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks demonstrate solid read-memory performance reaching 409.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks and steady in-memory key-value processing at 6.4 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle tiers, though write-heavy uncached memory bandwidth and cryptographic processing tests show lower relative efficiency. Lacking local disks and specialized vector acceleration flags, it is tailored for ARM-compatible memory-intensive tasks, intermediate database backends, caching services, and data transformation workloads.
